sections.label: Co-operative principles and registered co-ops
sections.summary: Co-ops operate on self-help and mutual assistance, with 79 registered today and about 80 serving roughly one million members.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: They operate on the principles of self-help and mutual assistance and are formed when individuals come together to address their common economic or social needs, or the needs identified in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: We have a total of 79 registered co-ops today, broadly categorised as credit co-ops and non-credit co-ops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Today, about 80 co-operatives serve approximately one million members across diverse sectors.

sections.label: Dividends and honoraria from reserves
sections.summary: The speaker commends the intent to let co-operative societies pay dividends and honoraria from reserves with the Registrar's approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, I commend the intent behind allowing co-operative societies to pay dividends and honoraria from their reserves, subject to the Registrar's approval.

sections.label: Reduction in by-law signatories
sections.summary: The proposed reduction in signatories for by-law amendment applications, from three to one, requires careful consideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The proposed reduction in signatories for by-law amendment applications, from three to one, requires careful consideration.

sections.label: Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act 2024
sections.summary: The Act is a significant legislative reform giving the co-operative movement flexibility, including paying dividends and honoraria from reserves with the Registrar's approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act 2024 is a significant legislative reform that impacts broader operations and provides flexibility to the co-operative movement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By allowing dividends and honoraria to be paid from reserves with the Registrar's approval, the Act acknowledges our need for greater operational flexibility.

sections.label: New section 72A on reserves
sections.summary: The introduction of the new section 72A specifies the allocation, distribution and payment of reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The introduction of the new section 72A, specifying the allocation, distribution, and payment of reserves, is particularly noteworthy.

sections.label: Registrar's approval in practice
sections.summary: The passage asks how obtaining the Registrar's approval for distributing dividends or paying from reserves will work in practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How will obtaining the Registrar's approval for distributing dividends or paying from reserves work in practice?

sections.label: Co-op dividends, bonds, debentures
sections.summary: Amendments let co-operatives pay dividends and honoraria from reserves with Registrar's approval and issue bonds and debentures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments, allowing co-operatives to pay dividends and honoraria from the reserves with the Registrar's approval, and issue bonds and debentures, will facilitate their growth and enhance benefits for their members.

sections.label: Credit co-op investment limit
sections.summary: A proposal to revisit the default 10% limit on credit co-ops' total assets for restricted investments approved by the Registrar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Regarding investment risk, I propose revisiting the default 10% limit on credit co-ops' total assets for investing in restricted investments approved by the Registrar.

sections.label: Progressive Workplace Grant recipients
sections.summary: The Progressive Workplace Grant, a one-off grant for adopting Tripartite Standards in 2023, was given to 25 co-operatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Progressive Workplace Grant, which provided a one-off grant for adopting the Tripartite Standards in 2023, has been given out to 25 co-operatives.

sections.label: Co-op membership numbers
sections.summary: Although there are only 80 co-ops, they have over one million members between them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Indeed, the widespread involvement in co-ops is indicated by the fact that although there are only 80 co-ops, they have between them, over one million members.

sections.label: Co-ops using reserves
sections.summary: Amendments address broadening co-ops' use of reserves, letting them distribute dividends or pay COM honoraria with the Registrar's approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments seek to address several key areas, including the broadening of the use of reserves by co-ops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Currently, co-ops face limitations in declaring dividends solely from the preceding year's surplus, which may not always align with their members' needs, especially in volatile environments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I have no objections to the amendments which would permit co-ops to use their reserves to distribute dividends to members or pay honoraria to members of the COM, subject to the approval of the Registrar of Co-operative Societies.

sections.label: By-law amendment signatories
sections.summary: Clause 5 reduces the signatories required for registering amendments to by-laws from three to one person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clause 5 reduces the number of signatories required for the registration of amendments to by-laws from three to one person.

sections.label: Registrar approval for co-op bonds
sections.summary: Clause 11 removes the Registrar's approval requirement for co-ops issuing bonds or debentures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Clause 11 removes the requirement for the Registrar's approval for the issuance of bonds or debentures by co-ops.

sections.label: Co-ops using reserves for dividends
sections.summary: Singapore has 79 co-ops, and the amendment seeks to let co-ops use reserves to pay dividends or honoraria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, there are 79 co-ops in Singapore, comprising consumer and service co-ops that provide goods and services to their members and credit co-ops that provide financial services, such as taking in deposits and granting loans to members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The current proposed amendment seeks to allow co-ops to use their reserves to pay dividends to members or pay honorarium to the Committee of Management.

sections.label: Credit co-ops below capital adequacy
sections.summary: Credit co-ops below the 10% Capital Adequacy Ratio face strict loan limits and need written approval to distribute dividends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Currently, credit co-ops that do not meet the minimum Capital Adequacy Ratio, or CAR, of 10% are bound by strict loan limits on unsecured general loans and must seek the Registrar's written approval to distribute dividends from that year's surplus.

sections.label: Shared secretariat for trade associations
sections.summary: The first item is to investigate creating a shared secretariat service to help smaller trade associations with limited resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, to investigate the feasibility of creating a shared secretariat service, modelled after the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce, to assist smaller trade associations (TAs) with limited resources.

sections.label: Dividends from reserves with approval
sections.summary: Co-ops may currently pay dividends only from the preceding year's surplus; the proposal allows tapping reserves with the Registrar's approval.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Currently, a co-op may only pay dividends from the preceding year's surplus.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We propose to allow them to tap their reserves to pay dividends and honoraria, subject to the Registrar's approval.

sections.label: Registrar's factors for dividend approval
sections.summary: The Registrar will consider rate reasonableness, compliance track records, governance strength, and prudential requirements, including minimum CAR after payment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The Registrar will also consider factors, like reasonableness of proposed rates compared to previous years, past compliance track records of the co-op's, strength of governance and particularly for credit co-ops, if these credit co-ops have met prudential requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Credit co-ops must also demonstrate that they can meet the prevailing minimum CAR after their proposed dividend or honoraria payment.

sections.label: Co-op dividend cap
sections.summary: A co-op must not pay a dividend on paid-up share or subscription capital exceeding 10% per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Under the current legislative framework, a co-op must not pay a dividend on paid-up share capital or subscription capital exceeding 10% per annum.

sections.label: General meeting amendment threshold
sections.summary: Amendments at a general meeting must be passed by at least three-quarters of members present and voting.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In the case of a general meeting, the resolution to make amendments must be passed by at least three-quarters of the members present and voting.

sections.label: CCF grants to co-ops
sections.summary: Over the last five years, CCF disbursed about $2.7 million in grants to co-ops.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Over the last five years, CCF disbursed about $2.7 million in grants to co-ops.

sections.label: SNCF courses and leaders programme
sections.summary: MCCY works with SNCF on an Audit Committee course in May 2024, and SNCF's 2022 Emerging Leaders Programme aims to groom 100 leaders in five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: MCCY for example is working with SNCF to introduce a new customised Audit Committee course for credit co-ops in May 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: SNCF has also established the Emerging Leaders Programme in 2022, which aims to groom 100 leaders in five years.

sections.label: Member approval and annual reports
sections.summary: Co-ops must obtain members' approval for COM benefits, with a proposed amendment making this an explicit AGM function, and in 2019 the Registrar notified co-ops of minimum annual report disclosures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: While co-ops must already obtain members’ approval for payment of allowance, honoraria and other benefits to the COM, we proposed amending the Act to make this an explicit function of the AGM.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In 2019, the Registrar also notified co-ops about the minimum information they need to disclose in an annual report to inform members about activities of the co-op and make informed decisions.

sections.label: Credit co-op regulation and advertising
sections.summary: Credit co-ops are not regulated like other financial institutions, are not open to the general public, and should not advertise in mass media.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: As a membership-based organisation, credit co-ops are not regulated to the same degree as other financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Hence, they are not open to the general public and should not advertise in mass media.

sections.label: Co-ops as social platform
sections.summary: Co-ops offer an additional platform for Singaporeans to come together and address evolving societal needs amid a refreshed social compact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In view of our refreshed social compact and renewed sense of social solidarity, co-ops indeed offer an additional platform for Singaporeans to come together and address societal evolving needs.

sections.label: Co-op total assets figure
sections.summary: The 2023 Registry of Co-operative Societies annual report states co-ops in Singapore hold $19.4 billion in total assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to the 2023 annual report published by the Registry of Co-operative Societies, co-ops in Singapore currently hold a staggering $19.4 billion worth of total assets.

sections.label: Annual ranking suggestion response
sections.summary: Responding to Mr Yong's annual ranking suggestion, the speaker notes co-ops have a spectrum of strengths, sizes, capabilities and governance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: On Mr Yong's suggestion for an annual ranking to identify co-ops that are better governed, as well as those that are weaker and which require more checks, earlier I mentioned that there is a spectrum of different strengths, sizes and capabilities and governance for co-ops.

sections.label: Registry monitoring and regulation
sections.summary: The Registry of Co-operative Societies has monitoring mechanisms and a differentiated regulatory approach, including special audits of credit co-ops and reviews of financial statements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The RCS does, in fact, have monitoring mechanisms in place to monitor co-ops and adopts a differentiated regulatory approach for co-ops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: To give you an example, the Registry conducts periodic special audits on credit co-ops and reviews the co-op's financial statements and annual reports to assess their financial health and their governance.
